text:
Ivar Stenberg went second overall in June, one pick after Gavin McKenna, and by late October the Sharks had him on their top line. He's 19 and has 16 points in 25 games, 0.64 a game. For forwards picked in the top four since 2005, the median first full season was 0.56.

Nine of those 16 points came on the power play, which is where his game lives right now. His goals are earned: 7.1 expected goals on his own shots (the quality of his chances), about one per 60 minutes. His 19.5% shooting is above his likely range, so a few fewer pucks should go in.

Five-on-five is the harder part. With him on the ice the Sharks get 43.8% of the expected goals, and they have scored 3.4 fewer goals than those chances deserved, so his even-strength points have been unlucky too. The line with Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith has had its nights, like the 4-2 win over Nashville when San Jose Hockey Now wrote that the kids are alright. Back home, he's up for a Swedish award. Not bad for a teenager on a young team.
headline: Ivar Stenberg, 19, is already a power-play weapon
